## ITAM

### Storytelling in Economics

::: {.eyebrow}
Master in Applied Economics · Spring 2025
:::

The course has two halves. One is the argument in Robert Shiller's
[*Narrative Economics*](https://press.princeton.edu/books/hardcover/9780691182292/narrative-economics):
economic stories spread through a population the way a disease does, and act as
shocks to real outcomes while they do. The other is the craft of explaining a
piece of empirical research to someone else, worked through real examples: what
to show, in what order, and in what words. Both halves answer to the same test.
The same result has to reach a technical audience, someone making a decision,
and a reader with no training in economics.

The [explainer](files/social-insurance-without-a-job-slides.html) for my job
market paper is the same craft applied to my own work. It walks a general
reader through the question, the method, and what the estimates can and
cannot say.

[Labor Market MX](/data.html) is the same craft applied to public data: the
ENOE series, one page per theme, with the charts carrying the point.

::: {.paper-links}
- [Course page](storytelling-in-economics.qmd)
:::
